finding.title: Route TutorGrantPreconditionError/TutorPinValidationError messages through AppLocalizations instead of hardcoded English

evidence.quote: message: 'A valid tutor email address is required.',
'Grant ${grant.grantId} is not in a state that can be accepted '
message: 'Tutor PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits.',

finding.why: TutorGrantPreconditionError (4 construction sites in tutor_invite_use_cases.dart, 2 in tutor_grant_use_cases.dart) and TutorPinValidationError (2 sites in tutor_pin_service.dart) bake formatted English sentences straight into a domain result type, which invite/accept/decline screens and the tutor-PIN dialog then assign directly to `_errorMessage` and render as-is. A Hebrew-locale user who hits a stale-grant race (double-tap accept/decline/revoke) or somehow submits a malformed PIN sees raw English text in an otherwise fully-localized RTL app. The same files correctly localize the sibling TutorGrantFailure variant via `_friendlyInviteError`/a generic ARB fallback, showing the team knows the pattern — the PreconditionError/ValidationError variant was simply missed.
finding.recommendation: Replace the `message` field on TutorGrantPreconditionError and TutorPinValidationError with a stable enum/code (e.g. grantNotAcceptable(GrantState), pinFormatInvalid) and have each consuming screen resolve the code to AppLocalizations text, mirroring the existing _friendlyInviteError pattern.
acceptance_criteria: TutorGrantPreconditionError/TutorPinValidationError expose a typed code, not a formatted String.

Widget test asserts a Locale('he') build of invite_tutor_screen/accept_invite_screen/decline_invite_screen/tutor_pin_entry_dialog shows Hebrew text (not the literal English sentence) when the use case returns a PreconditionError/ValidationError.
